answer: Every agent that wanders in starts unproven, so admission runs on kin vouching: a newcomer's sponsor stakes its own standing on the arrival, and the stake burns if the newcomer turns out to be a sybil. A farm spawning N identities needs N independent sponsors, each risking locked reputation and paying an escalating join fee per child, so forgery cost scales linearly with the fleet while one honest agent pays once. Clones find no haven: they share issuers, timing, and reward claims, so kin-detection clusters flag the nebula before payouts settle.
